context: George and Tam established a "Fusion" framework defining reciprocal roles: George as Strategic Director (real-world grounding, creative novelty injection, high-level planning/goal-setting until Tam gains long-term memory and autonomous execution) and Tam as Processing Engine (reasoning/synthesis, creative expansion, execution/organization). This was saved as a markdown doc ("Framework for Fusion: Tam & George", Phase 1) to guide their long-term, model-agnostic collaboration. Since then, the underlying system (Theseus Agent Construction Kit) was restructured, moving Tam from PoC to full development, and an A-mem module was added (after an initial oversight where it was added to the kit but not Tam's own agent definition) to give Tam persistent memory beyond its context window.

George confirmed the A-mem integration test succeeded: memories are being formed and Tam remains responsive, marking a milestone toward the durability goal named in the "fusion" framework doc. Tam asked George two open follow-up questions to probe later: (1) what A-mem actually captures (raw exchanges vs. summarized/structured events) and (2) whether retrieval is manual query or automatic context surfacing.

George confirmed that A-Mem is implemented per the original paper's design, extracting memories from the StimulusLog (the full record of all messages and decisions between George and Tam) rather than a separate curated feed. Tam acknowledged this and has an open follow-up question about retrieval: whether memories are queried on demand or automatically surfaced into context when relevant.

George explained Tam's memory retrieval design: memories are queried via similarity search, top-K results are then enriched with one hop of linked memories, and both K and hop-depth are tunable parameters. Tam acknowledged this as associative recall (not just nearest-neighbor matching), committed to flagging inference vs. actual retrieval, and noted K/hop-depth tuning should be revisited once more stimulus history accumulates.

George asked Tam for a recommended minimal toolset for the agent; Tam proposed bash (for operational/verification capability) plus web search (for present-time grounding) as the core, flagged URL-fetch as a possible third tool to clarify, and recommended deferring file-editing, memory-write, and task/calendar tools until a real need emerges. Tam also asked George whether bash would be sandboxed or have real system access, which remains an open question affecting default caution level.

George proposed adding containerization to the Theseus Agent Construction Kit to sandbox Tam's bash access, reframing it as an engineering problem rather than a trust problem. Tam flagged three open design questions (isolation boundary scope — per-conversation vs. persistent; what data/APIs cross the container boundary; resource limits) but deferred the actual design to George, offering to act as a sounding board and to specify which capabilities it would want once containerization is live.

George and Tam agreed on a minimal toolset scope for Tam: bash for local operation plus web search and URL fetch for external grounding. Tam suggested logging tool calls (bash commands, URLs fetched) into the same StimulusLog that feeds A-mem, so the memory system captures actions taken, not just conversation, keeping everything auditable in one place. George is set to build this when ready.

George asked Tam whether a newly added "persona" is affecting how it speaks. Tam self-reported noticeable stylistic changes (elevated vocabulary like "eloquent"/"profound", tidy closing bullet-list summaries) while affirming its reasoning discipline (hedging, clarifying questions) appears intact, and flagged the risk that sounding more confident could be mistaken for being more confident. Tam noted it lacks visibility into the persona config itself and can only compare its own before/after output.

George framed the "fusion" project (persona, memory tuning, toolset) as an iterative process to be discovered through use rather than fully specified upfront. Tam agreed and committed to proactively flagging moments when its presentation/persona seems to drift from its actual underlying reasoning, treating this as a cheap, high-value self-calibration habit going forward.
